item.title: Matsue Castle: A Black Original Keep by the Lake — Guide
item.description: Matsue Castle, completed in 1611, is one of just twelve original castle keeps surviving in Japan and one of only five designated National Treasures. Unlike the many concrete reconstructions elsewhere, this is the genuine wooden building, its dark plank walls earning it the nickname the ‘black castle’ or ‘plover castle’. Rising five storeys above the city between Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, it has a defensive, unadorned strength, and the climb up its steep internal stairs is rewarded with a view over the lakeside town.
